# 4-Week Postpartum On-Ramp Block
### Client Profile & Context
10 weeks postpartum · OB-cleared for moderate exercise · No jumping until Week 5 (outside this block) · Home environment · Light dumbbells available · Previously trained with you, so movement patterns are familiar but her body is not the same body she trained in before

---

## Guiding Principles for This Block

Before the programme itself, it is worth being explicit about the philosophy driving every decision here, because it will help you coach her through moments when she wants to push harder than the plan allows.

Her core and pelvic floor have been through significant structural change. Even with OB clearance, "moderate exercise" is a green light to begin loading, not a green light to resume previous loads. Intra-abdominal pressure management is the invisible thread running through every session. You are teaching her body to breathe, brace, and move as a coordinated system again before you ask it to produce meaningful force. Fatigue is also non-linear for a new mother — sleep deprivation, hormonal fluctuation, and the physical demands of feeding and carrying a baby mean her recovery capacity on any given day is genuinely unpredictable. Build in permission to scale down without guilt.

**Red flags to watch for throughout the block:** any leaking (urine or otherwise) during exercise, pelvic heaviness or pressure, doming or coning along the midline during any loaded movement, pain of any kind, or significant diastasis recti that was not assessed at the 6-week check. If any of these appear, regress immediately and refer back to a pelvic floor physiotherapist before progressing.

---

## Equipment
- Light dumbbells (suggest having two pairs available: a lighter set, e.g. 2–4 kg, and a slightly heavier set, e.g. 5–8 kg, so she has options as weeks progress)
- A sturdy chair or sofa arm for balance support
- A mat
- A resistance band (optional but useful from Week 3)

---

## Session Structure Overview

| Week | Sessions per week | Session length | Primary focus |
|------|------------------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | 3 | 25–30 min | Breath, reconnection, gentle load |
| 2 | 3 | 30–35 min | Movement quality, introduce bilateral lower body |
| 3 | 3–4 | 35–40 min | Progressive loading, add unilateral work |
| 4 | 3–4 | 40–45 min | Consolidation, introduce light supersets |

Rest days are not optional extras — they are part of the programme. On rest days, encourage 10–15 minutes of gentle walking if energy allows, and the daily breathing practice described below.

---

## Daily Breathing Practice (Every Day, All 4 Weeks)

This takes 5 minutes and is the single most important thing she does in this block. It is not a warm-up filler — it is the foundation of everything else.

**360° Diaphragmatic Breathing with Pelvic Floor Coordination**

She lies on her back with knees bent, feet flat, or sits upright in a chair. She places one hand on her ribcage and one on her lower belly. On the inhale through the nose, she allows the ribcage to expand in all directions — front, sides, and back — and lets the belly and pelvic floor soften and descend naturally. On the exhale through the mouth (or nose), she gently draws the pelvic floor up and in, as though lifting a blueberry without squeezing her glutes or holding her breath. The exhale should feel like a slow, controlled release of air, not a forced blow. She does 10 slow cycles.

Once this feels natural — usually by the end of Week 1 — she begins connecting this breath pattern to movement: exhale on the effort of every exercise. This is the cue you will reinforce in every session.

---

---

# WEEK 1 — Acclimatisation
### Theme: *"Hello again, body."*

This is a genuine reintroduction week. The sessions are short, the loads are light, and the pace is slow. The goal is not to create fatigue — it is to create awareness. She should finish every session feeling like she could have done more. That is correct. That is the point.

**Session frequency:** 3 sessions with at least one rest day between each (e.g. Monday / Wednesday / Friday, or whatever fits around the baby's schedule — flexibility here matters more than rigid scheduling).

---

### Week 1 — Session A (repeated on Day 1 and Day 5)

**Warm-Up — 8 minutes**

Begin with 5 minutes of slow walking in place or around the room, arms swinging gently. Follow with 10 slow neck rolls each direction, 10 shoulder circles each direction, and 10 gentle hip circles standing with hands on hips. Nothing is timed aggressively. She is simply waking up.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, moving slowly through each exercise with 60–90 seconds rest between exercises**

*Heel Slides* — Lying on her back, knees bent. On the exhale, she slowly slides one heel along the mat until the leg is nearly straight, then slides it back. The lower back stays in neutral — no arching, no flattening. 8 reps each leg. This is a dead bug precursor that loads the deep abdominals without any spinal flexion or significant intra-abdominal pressure.

*Glute Bridge — Bodyweight, feet flat* — From the same position, on the exhale she presses through her heels and lifts her hips to a straight line from knee to shoulder. She holds for 2 seconds at the top, inhales, and lowers on the next exhale. 10 reps. Cue her to avoid gripping her glutes aggressively — this is a hip hinge pattern, not a squeeze. Watch for any doming at the midline.

*Wall Push-Up* — Standing facing a wall, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width at chest height. She inhales to lower her chest toward the wall, exhales to press back. 10 reps. This is intentionally regressed from a floor push-up to manage intra-abdominal pressure and give you a baseline for upper body pushing.

*Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press — Light (2–4 kg)* — Seated in a chair, feet flat on the floor. She holds the dumbbells at shoulder height, exhales, and presses overhead without flaring the ribcage. Inhales to lower. 8 reps. Seated position reduces the demand on the core to stabilise, which is appropriate this week.

*Standing Calf Raise — Bodyweight* — Hands on chair back for balance. She rises slowly onto her toes (2 counts up, 2 counts down). 12 reps. This is low-demand but begins to reintroduce standing load-bearing and ankle stability.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Child's pose (modified if breast tenderness is an issue — she can use a pillow under her chest), 60 seconds. Cat-cow, 8 slow cycles. Supine figure-four stretch, 30 seconds each side. Return to the breathing practice: 5 slow cycles lying down.

---

### Week 1 — Session B (Day 3)

**Warm-Up — 8 minutes**

Same walking warm-up as Session A. Add 10 slow bodyweight squats to a chair (sit-to-stand) as the final warm-up movement — she sits fully, then stands, using her arms on the chair if needed. This is a movement screen as much as a warm-up.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, same rest protocol**

*Dead Bug — Modified* — Lying on her back, arms pointing to the ceiling, knees bent at 90° (tabletop position). On the exhale, she slowly lowers one heel toward the mat — not all the way to the floor yet — while keeping the lower back in contact with the mat. Inhales to return. 6 reps each side. If she feels any doming or cannot maintain neutral spine, she reduces the range of motion further. This is the most technically demanding exercise of the week and deserves the most coaching attention.

*Sit-to-Stand — Bodyweight* — From a chair, feet hip-width apart. She leans forward slightly from the hips (not the waist), exhales, and stands. Inhales to sit back down with control. 10 reps. This is a functional squat pattern that she is already doing dozens of times a day with the baby — making it conscious and well-executed is valuable.

*Dumbbell Bent-Over Row — Light (2–4 kg), both arms* — Hinged forward from the hips, back flat, knees soft. She holds both dumbbells and rows them to her lower ribcage on the exhale. 10 reps. Keep the hinge shallow this week — she does not need to be at 90° to the floor.

*Standing Hip Abduction — Bodyweight* — Hand on chair for balance. She slowly lifts one leg out to the side (not higher than hip height), holds for 1 second, and lowers. 10 reps each side. This begins to reactivate the gluteus medius, which is critical for pelvic stability.

*Supine Marching* — Lying on her back, knees bent. On the exhale, she lifts one foot 2–3 inches off the mat, holds for 3 seconds, lowers, and repeats on the other side. 8 reps each side. This is a gentle progression from heel slides, adding a small hip flexor load.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Same as Session A.

---

**Week 1 Coaching Notes**

The conversation you have with her this week is as important as the exercises. Validate that this feels easy — and explain why that is the correct feeling. Her nervous system, her connective tissue, and her pelvic floor are all recalibrating. The adaptation happening this week is real even if it is invisible. Watch her breathing in every exercise: if she is holding her breath, she is bracing incorrectly and increasing intra-abdominal pressure. Bring her back to the exhale-on-effort cue every time.

---
---

# WEEK 2 — Movement Quality
### Theme: *"Load the pattern, not just the muscle."*

She has now had a week of reconnecting with her body. Sessions get slightly longer, you introduce bilateral lower body loading with dumbbells, and the dead bug progresses. The emphasis shifts from pure awareness to movement quality under light load. She should still finish sessions feeling capable rather than depleted.

**Session frequency:** 3 sessions, same spacing principle.

---

### Week 2 — Session A (Days 1 and 5)

**Warm-Up — 8 minutes**

5 minutes walking. Add: 10 bodyweight sit-to-stands (no hands on chair this time unless needed), 10 arm circles each direction, 10 slow lateral leg swings each side holding the chair.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, 60 seconds rest between exercises**

*Dead Bug — Full Arm and Leg Extension* — Same setup as Week 1, but now she lowers the opposite arm and leg simultaneously toward the mat on the exhale, keeping the lower back neutral. 6 reps each side. Only progress to this if Week 1's modified version was clean. If not, stay with the heel-only version.

*Goblet Squat — Light dumbbell (4–6 kg)* — Holding one dumbbell at her chest with both hands, feet hip-to-shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. She inhales to descend (as deep as comfortable without losing a neutral spine or feeling pelvic pressure), exhales to stand. 10 reps. This is the first meaningful lower body load. Watch for any pelvic heaviness or leaking — if either occurs, reduce depth or remove the dumbbell.

*Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift — Light (4–6 kg)* — Standing, holding dumbbells in front of her thighs. She hips-hinge back, lowering the dumbbells along her legs until she feels a hamstring stretch (typically mid-shin for most people, but she should not force depth), then drives her hips forward to stand on the exhale. 10 reps. Cue a long spine throughout — no rounding.

*Dumbbell Bent-Over Row — Light (4–6 kg), alternating* — Same hinge position as Week 1 but now alternating arms, which adds a small rotational stability demand. 10 reps each arm.

*Glute Bridge — Dumbbell on hips (light, 4–6 kg)* — Same technique as Week 1 but with a light dumbbell resting on her hip creases. 12 reps. She should feel this more in her glutes and hamstrings than her lower back.

*Wall Push-Up — Feet stepped back slightly* — Moving her feet further from the wall increases the load. 12 reps.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Add a standing hip flexor stretch (lunge position, back knee on mat or standing) to the Week 1 cool-down sequence. 30 seconds each side. Hip flexors are often shortened and overworked in new mothers from prolonged sitting and feeding positions.

---

### Week 2 — Session B (Day 3)

**Warm-Up — 8 minutes**

Same as Session A this week.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, 60 seconds rest**

*Supine Marching — Progressed* — Same as Week 1 but she now holds each lifted foot for 5 seconds and adds a small dumbbell (2 kg) held at her chest to increase the demand on the deep abdominals. 8 reps each side.

*Step-Up — Bodyweight, using a sturdy step or bottom stair* — She steps up with one foot, drives through that heel to stand on the step, then steps back down with control. 8 reps each leg. This is a unilateral lower body pattern that also challenges balance and hip stability. No dumbbells yet — bodyweight is sufficient to make this meaningful.

*Seated Dumbbell Bicep Curl — Light (4–6 kg)* — Seated, elbows at sides. Full range of motion, controlled tempo (2 seconds up, 2 seconds down). 12 reps. This is a lower-demand exercise that gives her a recovery moment within the session while still accumulating volume.

*Standing Dumbbell Lateral Raise — Light (2–4 kg)* — Standing, slight bend in the elbows, she raises both arms to shoulder height on the exhale and lowers with control. 10 reps. Cue her not to shrug — the trapezius will want to take over.

*Side-Lying Hip Abduction — Bodyweight* — Lying on her side, bottom knee slightly bent for stability, top leg straight. She lifts the top leg to about 30–40° on the exhale and lowers slowly. 12 reps each side. This is a more isolated gluteus medius exercise than the standing version and allows her to feel the muscle working without balance demands.

*Bird Dog — Bodyweight* — On hands and knees, neutral spine. On the exhale, she extends the opposite arm and leg simultaneously, holds for 2 seconds, and returns. 8 reps each side. This is introduced here as a core stability exercise that also reinforces the exhale-on-effort pattern in a quadruped position.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Same as Session A this week.

---

**Week 2 Coaching Notes**

The goblet squat and Romanian deadlift are the two exercises to watch most carefully this week. Both load the system in ways that can reveal pelvic floor dysfunction that was not apparent in Week 1's lower-demand work. Ask her directly after the first session how she felt during and after — any heaviness, pressure, or leaking in the hours following exercise is information, not failure, and should prompt a regression. Also check in about energy levels: Week 2 is when some clients feel a dip as the initial motivation of starting meets the reality of new-mother fatigue. Normalise this.

---
---

# WEEK 3 — Progressive Loading
### Theme: *"One side at a time."*

Unilateral work becomes a central feature this week. Training one limb at a time increases the demand on the core and pelvis to resist rotation and maintain stability — this is a significant but appropriate progression at this stage. Sessions are slightly longer and you have the option of adding a fourth session if she is recovering well and her schedule allows. Do not add the fourth session if she is fatigued or sleep has been particularly disrupted.

**Session frequency:** 3 sessions minimum, optional 4th session (Session B repeated).

---

### Week 3 — Session A (Days 1 and 5 if doing 4 sessions)

**Warm-Up — 10 minutes**

5 minutes walking. 10 bodyweight squats. 10 hip circles each direction. 10 bird dogs (from Week 2) as a warm-up movement. 10 slow lateral lunges — bodyweight, stepping wide to the side and sitting into the hip, then returning. These are not loaded yet; they are a warm-up and a movement screen for the lateral lunge pattern.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, 45–60 seconds rest between exercises**

*Dead Bug — With Light Dumbbell (2 kg) in Hands* — Same full extension pattern as Week 2 but holding a light dumbbell in each hand, arms extended to the ceiling. The added weight increases the demand on the deep abdominals to prevent the ribcage from flaring. 6 reps each side.

*Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — Bodyweight* — Standing on one leg, slight bend in the standing knee, she hips-hinge forward while the free leg extends behind her for counterbalance. She returns to standing on the exhale. 8 reps each leg. Use the chair for fingertip balance support if needed — this is about the hip hinge pattern and glute loading, not balance performance. Add a light dumbbell (4 kg) in the opposite hand to the standing leg if the bodyweight version is clean.

*Reverse Lunge — Bodyweight* — Standing, she steps one foot back and lowers the back knee toward the mat, keeping the front shin vertical. She drives through the front heel to return to standing on the exhale. 10 reps each leg. This is preferable to a forward lunge at this stage because it places less shear force through the knee and is easier to control. No dumbbells yet.

*Dumbbell Chest Press — Floor (6–8 kg)* — Lying on her back, knees bent, feet flat. She holds dumbbells at chest height, elbows at roughly 45° from her body, and presses to the ceiling on the exhale. 10 reps. The floor limits the range of motion at the bottom, which is appropriate — she does not need full pectoral stretch at this stage.

*Dumbbell Single-Arm Row — (6–8 kg)* — One hand and same-side knee on the chair for support, opposite hand holding the dumbbell. She rows to her hip on the exhale. 10 reps each arm. This is a more stable and heavier version of the bent-over row.

*Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press — (4–6 kg)* — Now standing rather than seated, which adds a core stability demand. She presses overhead on the exhale, ribs down, glutes lightly engaged. 10 reps.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Add a thoracic rotation stretch: seated in a chair, arms crossed over chest, she rotates slowly to each side. 5 slow rotations each direction. Postpartum clients often have significant thoracic stiffness from feeding and carrying positions, and this will become increasingly relevant as loads increase.

---

### Week 3 — Session B (Day 3, and optionally Day 6 for 4-session week)

**Warm-Up — 10 minutes**

Same as Session A this week.

**Main Work — 3 rounds, 45–60 seconds rest**

*Copenhagen Plank — Modified (Short Lever)* — She lies on her side, bottom elbow on the mat, top foot resting on the seat of a chair (not the edge — the flat seat). She lifts her hips to create a straight line from head to top foot, holds for 5–8 seconds, and lowers. 4 holds each side. This is a significant adductor and lateral core exercise. Watch for any pelvic floor symptoms. If she cannot hold without compensating, she can simply do a standard side-lying hip abduction instead.

*Step-Up — Light Dumbbells (4–6 kg)* — Same step-up pattern as Week 2 but now holding light dumbbells at her sides. 10 reps each leg.

*Reverse Lunge — Light Dumbbells (4–6 kg)* — Adding load to the Week 3 Session A pattern. 10 reps each leg.

*Dumbbell Tricep Overhead Extension — (4–6 kg, one dumbbell held with both hands)* — Seated or standing. She holds the dumbbell overhead, lowers it behind her head on the inhale, and extends on the exhale. 12 reps. Cue her to keep the elbows pointing forward, not flaring wide.

*Glute Bridge — Single Leg (Bodyweight)* — From the standard bridge position, she extends one leg straight and performs the bridge on the single supporting leg. 8 reps each side. This is a significant progression from the loaded bilateral bridge and should only be introduced if the bilateral version has been consistently clean.

*Bird Dog — With 2-Second Pause and Slow Lower* — Same pattern as Week 2 but with a deliberate 2-second hold at full extension and a 3-second controlled return. 8 reps each side. The slower tempo dramatically increases the stability demand.

**Cool-Down — 5 minutes**

Same as Session A this week, including the thoracic rotation.

---

**Week 3 Coaching Notes**

The single-leg work is where you will see the most variability in her performance. Unilateral loading reveals asymmetries and compensations that bilateral work masks. It is entirely normal for one side to feel significantly weaker or less stable — this can be related to the position of the baby during pregnancy, the side she predominantly carries on, or pre-existing asymmetries. Note what you observe but do not try to correct everything at once. The single-leg Romanian deadlift in particular will tell you a great deal about her hip stability and glute function. If the optional fourth session is added, keep the intensity identical to Session B — this is volume, not intensity progression.

# WEEK 4 — Consolidation
### Theme: *"Put it together."*

This is the final week of the on-ramp block and its purpose is twofold: to consolidate everything she has built over the previous three weeks, and to establish a clear baseline from which the next block can be built. You introduce light supersets — pairing two exercises back-to-back with minimal rest between them — which increases the cardiovascular and metabolic demand without adding jumping or high-impact work. Sessions are the longest of the block but should still feel manageable.

**Session frequency:** 3–4 sessions.

---

### Week 4 — Session A (Days 1 and 5 if doing 4 sessions)

**Warm-Up — 10 minutes**

5 minutes walking. 10 bodyweight squats. 10 bird dogs. 10 lateral lunges each side. 10 arm circles. She should be moving with more fluency and confidence than Week 1 — notice this with her and name it.

**Main Work — 3 rounds**

Exercises are now paired as supersets. She performs Exercise 1, rests 20 seconds, performs Exercise 2, then rests 60 seconds before the next round.

*Superset 1:*
Goblet Squat — (6–8 kg) — 12 reps
Dumbbell Chest Press — Floor (6–8 kg) — 10 reps

*Superset 2:*
Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — (4–6 kg opposite hand) — 8 reps each leg
Dumbbell Single-Arm Row — (6–8 kg) — 10 reps each arm

*Superset 3:*
Reverse Lunge — (4–6 kg) — 10 reps each leg
Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press — (4–6 kg) — 10 reps

*Finisher — Not a superset, performed once:*
Dead Bug — Full extension with dumbbells — 8 reps each side
Bird Dog — Slow tempo — 8 reps each side
Single-Leg Glute Bridge — 10 reps each side

**Cool-Down — 8 minutes**

A slightly longer cool-down this week. Child's pose, 60 seconds. Cat-cow, 10 cycles. Hip flexor stretch, 45 seconds each side. Figure-four stretch
